and separate possession of her 1/3rd share in the suit schedule properties and further to declare that

her 1/3rd share in the suit schedule properties.

2. Brief facts of the case Late T. Velayudhan, is the father of the plaintiff and the
father-in-law of the Defendant Nos. 1 and 4. Said T. Velayudhan married Smt.
Kanthamma and within their wedlock they had three children namely, the plaintiff,
husband of defendant No.1, Venkatesh V. and the husband of defendant No.4
namely, V. Dorai Kanna.The defendant 2 & 3 are the minor children of Late
Venkatesh V. The plaintiff and defendants constitute a undivided Hindu Joint family
of Late Velayudhan and are governed by the provisions of the Mithakshara School of
Law. During the lifetime of said Velayudhan he had inherited certain property from
his ancestors in property bearing Survey Nos. 67 sub Division No. 2M-30 cents,
Survey Nos. 67 sub Division No. 2H-70 cents, Survey Nos. 68 sub Division No. 10-40
cents, and in Survey Nos. 68 sub Division No. 13-40 cents, in all measuring 180 cents,
situated at Madhandakuppam Village, Katpadi Town Taluk, Vellore C/W O.S.No.
4177/2020 District, Tamil Nadu, described as Item No. 1 of the suit schedule
property.
It is the further case of the plaintiff that item No.2 of the suit schedule property was purchased by
Sri Velayudhan under the registered Sale Deed, dated 23.10.1974, from one Sri MK Puttabuddi son
of Kullappa and later the said property was again conveyed by the BDA to the Plaintiff's father under
a registered Sale Deed dated 28.03.1983. while item No.3 was purchased by the mother Smt.
Kanthamma under the Sale Deed, dated 13.12.1971. According to the plaintiff Smt. Kanthamma had
expressed her intention to give away item No.3 of the suit schedule property to the plaintiff as
Sthreedhana property. However, Smt. Kanthamma died intestate without executing any instrument
in favour of the plaintiff. Meanwhile the father of the plaintiff after the death of his wife Smt.
Kanthamma without the knowledge and consent of the plaintiff got item No.3 of the property
transferred in his name. It is averred C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 that the BDA had also executed
Transfer Agreement in favour of Sri Velayudhan. In this manner Sri Velayudhan has acquired title to
item No.1 to 3 of the schedule properties.
It is further submitted by the plaintiff that somewhere in 2003 Sri Velayudhan did not have funds to
develop the property and therefore, he had requested the husband of the plaintiff to add his own
costs with an understanding that he may use the property for his exclusive benefit in future. Relying
on the representation of Sri Velayudhan, the husband of the plaintiff invested his hard earned
money and constructed two floors with two bed room house and after completion of construction
the father of the plaintiff mutually divided the property by giving ground floor to Venkatesh, first
floor to Dorai Kannan and 2 nd floor to the plaintiff. Hence, from the said date they are in the

separate possession of their respective shares.
C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 On 02.10.2019 Sri Venkatesh died leaving behind the defendants No.1 to 3
while on 22.05.2015 Dorai Kannan died leaving behind the defendant No.4. According to the
plaintiff, the defendant No.4 had filed O.S.No. 2375/2017 seeking eviction of the husband of the
defendant No.1. Meanwhile the plaintiff intervened and advised the defendant No.4 to withdraw the
suit by intimating her to affect partition in the joint family properties. The defendant No.4 though
agreed to withdraw the suit and affect partition, but surprisingly instituted the suit in O.S.No.
647/2019 against the plaintiff and defendants No.1 to 3 for the relief of declaration and possession
by claiming her right on the basis of the alleged Will dated 10.11.2010. Initially the defendant No.4
had agreed to withdraw the suit and affect partition, but later on she refused to withdraw the suit
and therefore, the plaintiff has approached this court.
C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 According to the plaintiff, the Will executed by Sri Velayudhan is without
any absolute title over item No.1 as it was purchased out of nucleus of the joint family. The alleged
Will executed by Sri Velayudhan is a fabricated document by defendant No.4 and as such it is not
binding on the plaintiff. Under the Will item No.2 is bequeathed to Sri Dorai Kannan and item No.3
is bequeathed to Sri Venkatesh. It is averred that Item No.3 was acquired by mother of the plaintiff
and after her death, Sri Velayudhan had obtained Transfer Agreement from BDA. The plain reading
of the Transfer Agreement would reveal that item No.3 is the self acquired property of Smt.
Kanthamma and same was inherited by Sri Velayudhan by way of succession. The Will executed by
Sri Velayudhan is shrouded with suspicious circumstances as Sri Velayudhan was aged, sick and
infirm at the time of execution of the Will. Thus, neither the defendant No.4 nor the defendants No.1
to 3 derive any independent title over C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 the properties bequeathed under the
Will. Thus, the said Will was obtained by playing fraud on the plaintiff. In fact, the husband of the
defendant No.1 namely Sri Venkatesh had denied the alleged Will when he was contesting the suit
filed by the defendant No.4. Now, only with an intention to deprive the legitimate right of the
plaintiff, the husband of the defendant No.4 has created the alleged Will. Thus, sought to decree the
suit.
3. In response to the suit summons, the defendants appeared through their counsel.the defendant
No.1 has filed common written-statement on behalf of defendants No.2 & 3 by admitting the
relationship between the parties and the mode of acquisition of the suit schedule properties.
However, the defendant No.1has taken the following contentions. There was a family arrangement
prior to the execution of the registered Will under which item No.1 was allotted to the husband of
the defendant No.1 and C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 therefore, the plaintiff is not entitled to item No.1.
Item No.2 of the suit schedule property was purchased by the father of the plaintiff and hence, it is
the self acquired property of the father of the plaintiff. similarly, item No.3 was purchased out of the
income of the father of the plaintiff in the name of his wife Smt. Kanthamma, who was only a
housewife and had no independent source of income. After the death of Smt. Kanthamma, Sri
Velayudhan acquired title over item No.3 as per the own admission of the plaintiff. Hence, the
contention of the plaintiff that item No.3 is the self acquired property of Kantamma is incorrect. Sri
Velayudhan was hale and healthy at the time of execution of the Will. After the demise of Sri
Velayudhan, Venaktesh and Dorai Kannan, the defendants No.1 to 3 are in joint possession of item

No.1. The defendants No.1 to 3 have admitted the institution of O.S.No. 647/2019 by defendant No.4
against the defendants No.1 to 3. The defendants No.1 to 3 have C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 contended
that another property bearing No.23 acquired by the father of the plaintiff in the name of Smt.
Kanthamma was given to the plaintiff under the registered release deed on 19.03.2009 and the
plaintiff has suppressed about the execution of the registered release deed. The plaintiff has already
been given her share in terms of the registered release deed and the said fact has already been
disclosed in the Will dated 10.11.2011. Therefore, the plaintiff has no locus standi to challenge the
Will. It is clearly stated in the Will that item No.1 of the suit property situated at Tamil Nadu is given
to Venkatesh, the husband of the 1 st defendant and Dorai Kannan, the husband of 4 th defendant.
Thus, the plaintiff is not entitled to any share in item No.1 of the schedule properties. It is further
contended that the plaintiff has not incorporated the boundaries of item No.1 in the plaint and the
said fact demonstrates that the plaintiff at no point of time was in joint possession and enjoyment of
item No.1. It is further C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 averred that item No.3 of the suit schedule property
has been bequeathed in favour of the husband of the defendant No.1 and he was in exclusive
possession and enjoyment. After his demise, the defendants No.1 to 3 are in enjoyment of the same.
Sri Velayudhan was a plumbing contractor and he was running his plumbing work in the name of
M/s. Dorai Kannan Plumbing Works and out his self earnings, he had purchased item Nos.2 and 3
and also property bearing No.23, which is the subject matter of release deed. The father of the
plaintiff was in sound disposing state of mind at the time of execution of the will deed and sought to
dismiss the suit.
The defendant No.4 has filed a separate written- statement admitting the relationship between the
parties. She has also averred that property No.23 has been gifted by Sri Velayudhan to the plaintiff.
After the death of Smt. Kanthamma, Sri Velayudhan had no right to execute the gift deed in favour
of the plaintiff in relation to the aforesaid C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 property. The plaintiff ought to
have included the said property in the suit, but the plaintiff has not included it and hence, the suit is
not maintainable. It is averred that Velayudhan had constructed and developed item No.2 of the
property and therefore, the contention of the plaintiff that her husband developed item No.2 of the
property is denied. The plaintiff and her husband are residing in a separate residence and therefore,
the entire claim that she is residing in item No.2 of the suit schedule property is denied. When the
husband of defendant No.1 started creating nuisance to defendant No.4 and also occupied item No.2
unauthorizedly, she filed a suit, which was withdrawn subsequently and now she has filed a suit for
declaration and possession in respect of item No.2 in O.S.No. 647/2019. Neither the plaintiff nor the
defendants No.1 to 3 have any right over item No.2 of the suit schedule property, since it is the self
acquired property of Sri Velayudhan and it has been bequeathed to the husband of C/W O.S.No.
4177/2020 defendant No.4. After the death of husband of defendant No.4, the defendant No.4 is the
absolute owner and in possession of the said property. The defendant No.4 has obtained katha and
other revenue records from BBMP and has obtained water and electricity connection. The plaintiff
and her husband had no source of income and they were residing with the family of Sri Velayudhan
and other defendants. Hence, sought to dismiss the suit.

647/2019, who is the defendant NO.4 in O.S.No. 4177/2020 seeking the following reliefs:

5. The brief facts of the case in O.S.No. 647/2019, are as under:
The plaintiff is owner of the suit schedule property bearing No.7, Old No. 842, 5th A
cross Road, BSK 1 st Stage II block, Bengaluru consisting of ground floor, first and
second floor. Originally the suit schedule property was owned by the father in law of
the plaintiff Sri T. Velayudan son of Dondu Muniswamy Mudaliar and it was
purchased from one Sri M.K. Puttabuddi, son of Kullappa under the registered sale
deed dated 23.10.1974. Later on Sri T. Velayudan had got another sale deed from
BDA on 28.03.1983. The father in law of the plaintiff had got the revenue documents
transferred in his name and had got constructed ground floor plus two floors in the
suit schedule property. During his lifetime he was in peaceful C/W O.S.No.
4177/2020 possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.
The father in law of the plaintiff had executed registered Will on 10.11.2010. As per the Will, the suit
schedule property has been bequeathed in favour of Dorai Kannan, who is the husband of the
plaintiff herein and another property was bequeathed in favour of defendant No.1 namely Sri
Venkatesh. It is further contended that during the lifetime of Sri T. Velayudan he had gifted another
property to defendant No.2 by way of gift deed. Sri T. Velayudan died on 11.11.2012 and the husband
of the plaintiff died on 22.05.2015. After the death of the husband of the plaintiff, the plaintiff had
obtained katha and revenue documents from BBMP in her name and has paid up to date taxes and
also obtained water and BESCOM connection in her name. During the lifetime of the father in law,
the family of the plaintiff, defendants No.1 and 2 were residing in the suit schedule property, but
after his demise, the husband of the plaintiff demanded the C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 defendants

requested the defendants No.1 and 2 to vacate, and hand over the possession of the suit property but

receipt of the notice, they failed to comply the demands made in the notice and hence, this suit.
6. The defendant No.1 has filed separate written- statement contending that the Will relied upon by
the plaintiff dated 10.11.2010 has not at all been probated and therefore, the suit is not
maintainable. The defendant No.1 has admitted that Sri T. Velayudhan had executed a gift deed in
favour of the defendant No.2, but has denied the claim of ownership of the plaintiff on the basis of
the Will C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 and the revenue documents obtained in her name. He has
admitted that the plaintiff and the defendants were residing together during the lifetime of Sri T.
Velayudhan, but has denied the request made by the plaintiff to quit and handover the possession.
He has further admitted that he is in possession of the ground floor portion, excluding one room
and the defendant No.2 is in possession of the 2 nd floor. It is further contended that the suit of the
plaintiff is not maintainable and there is no landlord and tenant relationship between the plaintiff

mentally stable and that Sri T. Velayudhan was finding difficult to identify even the family members

T. C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 Velayudhan had requested the husband of defendant No.2 to develop the
suit schedule property at his own costs and had permitted him to reap the benefits in the suit

It is further contended that she had no obligation to allow the plaintiff to reside in the suit schedule

properties in respect of Sri T. Velayudhan as he had no power to execute the Will. Hence, sought to
dismiss the suit. The defendant no.3 was placed ex parte on 15.3.2019.

11. ISSUE Nos.1 TO 3 IN O.S.No.4177/2020:-
These issues are interconnected and therefore, they are taken up together for
common discussion to avoid repetition of facts.
12. The relationship between the parties is not in dispute. The plaintiff in O.S.No. 4177/2020 has
sought the relief of partition and separate possession in item Nos.1 to 3 of the suit schedule
properties to the extent of her 1/3rd share. Meanwhile, the plaintiff in O.S.No. 647/2019 has
claimed the relief of declaration to declare that she is the absolute ownership of item No.2 of the
plaint schedule property in O.S.No. 4177/2020, which is the only suit schedule property in O.S.No.
647/2019 and further to decare that the defendants are in the unauthorised C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020
occupation of the suit property and to direct them to hand over the possession of the suit property.
13. In the first place this court is required to examine the nature of the suit properties and their
mode of acquisition by Velayuddan to ascertain the rival claims of the parties in O.S.NO.4177/2020

32. No doubt the limitation for a suit for declaration is provided under Part III of the Schedule to the
Limitation Act, 1963. It is governed by Articles 56-58 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act. Under
all the aforesaid three Articles, the limitation for a suit for declaration is three years from the date
when the right to sue first accrues. In the case at hand, the suit is not simply for the declaration of
title rather it is for a further relief for recovery of possession. It C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 is to be
noted that when in a suit for declaration of title, a further relief is claimed in addition to mere
declaration, the relief of declaration would only be an ancillary one and for the purposes of
limitation, it would be governed by the relief that has been additionally claimed. The further relief
claimed in the suit is for recovery of possession based upon title and as such its limitation would be
12 years in terms of Article 65 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act.
33 . In C. Mohammad Yunus vs. Syed Unnissa And Ors, AIR 1961 SC 808, it has been laid down that
in a suit for declaration with a further relief, the limitation would be governed by the Article
governing the suit for such further relief. In fact, a suit for a declaration of title to immovable
property would not be barred so long as the right to such a property continues and subsists. When
such right continues to subsist, the relief for declaration would be a continuing right and there
would be no limitation for such C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 a suit. The principle is that the suit for a
declaration for a right cannot be held to be barred so long as right to property subsists.
34. Thus it is clear from the conjoint reading of Article 65 of the Limitation Act and the ratio laid
down by the Apex Court in the aforesaid judgments that in a suit of this nature if the question of
limitation is raised by the defendants, he must have taken a plea with regard to his possession being
adverse to the possession of the plaintiff and if the suit of the plaintiff is based on his title, the
correct Article applicable is 65 and not Article 59. As such, in the instant case also in the absence of
plea of adverse possession and the suit being filed within 12 years from the date of death of
